title: Edge limiter warmup, graceful handoff and SLO-preserving degradation
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: When regional limiter instances or edge proxies fail or restart we observe sharp request drops, unfair redistributions of burst capacity, and p99 latency regressions for tail-sensitive tenants. This ticket proposes a coordinated warmup + graceful handoff protocol at the edge that preserves SLOs during limiter outages and restarts while maintaining fairness across tenants and bursty clients.
acceptance_criteria: 1) During simulated edge limiter restart, P99 latency for high-priority tenants increases by <= 10% and availability loss <= 0.05% (compared to baseline). 2) No tenant experiences >20% sudden request drop relative to steady-state burst allowance during a handoff. 3) Observability exposes clear handoff traces and metrics (handoff_duration_ms, shadow_allowance, admission_gradient). 4) Rollout gated by chaos test results and monitoring alerts.
design_summary: Introduce an edge-side warmup window and soft handoff where a restarting limiter shadow-accepts requests for a short period and advertises a conservative admission gradient. Key components: (a) warmup token reservoir: a small, time-decayed pool that accumulates slowly while instance is healthy and is used to bootstrap after restart; (b) graceful handoff window: leaderless, time-bounded co-admission where both old and new proxies accept with a weighted gradient; (c) admission gradient curve: per-tenant ramp function (0..1) that limits sudden bursts; (d) fairness governor: short-lived proportional credits to account for lost in-flight requests during handoff; (e) circuit-break scoring: integrate handoff into existing circuit-break mechanism so that a region-level fallback is triggered only after handoff completes or fails repeatedly.
implementation_notes: - Add lightweight shadow-mode to edge proxy: accept and enqueue decision but mark metric 'shadow_accepted' to avoid double-billing. - Warmup reservoir persisted in local ephemeral storage with TTL-based decay so restarts within small windows can resume partial state. - Admission gradients computed from recent RPS distribution and tenant weight; default 30s linear ramp. - Credit rebalancer will issue proportional short-term credits to tenants suffering drops, bounded by emergency budget.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: edge.handoff.duration_ms, edge.handoff.shadow_accept_rate, edge.warmup.reservoir_size, edge.admission.gradient_current, edge.fairness.credit_issued. Alerts: handoff_duration > 10s in a single region, shadow_accept_rate > 1% for >5m, sudden credit issuance spike > threshold. Dashboards: handoff waterfall with traces linking proxy restarts, shadow accept events, credit issuance, and client observed latency.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'edge_warmup_handoff' (off by default). 2) Canary enable on internal tenants in us-west-2 for 48h. 3) Gradual 10%→50%→100% route weight rollout across regions if canary stable. 4) Monitor SLO guardrails; immediate rollback on increased p99 > threshold or credit budget exhaustion. 5) Post-rollout 7-day watch with oncall playbook.
testing_and_simulation: - Unit tests for reservoir decay, gradient calculation, and credit rebalancer. - Integration tests for dual-proxy co-admission and idempotency. - Chaos simulation: repeated proxy restarts under mixed bursty client patterns; validate acceptance criteria. - Load test: synthetic tenants with skewed weight profiles to verify fairness governor operates within budget.
open_questions: What is the per-tenant emergency credit cap? (suggest starting at 5% of monthly burst budget)
Should warmup reservoir persist to S3 for longer restarts or is local ephemeral TTL sufficient?
How to surface shadow-accepts in SDKs so customers can opt-in for replay debugging?
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed comparing linear vs exponential warmup curves; linear 30s chosen for predictability.
2026-03-04: Implemented prototype shadow-mode in local dev; initial metrics emitted for shadow_accept_rate.
2026-03-08: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-15 on internal tenants; PR opened for review (link above).
notes_for_oncall: If handoff_duration alert fires, set feature flag off for region and follow Isolate→Restore runbook. If credit budget exhausted, enable regional fallback to alternative model variant until stabilization.
